---
title: "Setting up Python"
page-layout: article
---

The examples are tested with Python 3.12 and the package versions in `requirements.txt`.
We use conda for the environment and pip for the packages. From the repository root, run

```bash
conda create -n estimating-hank-nn python=3.12
conda activate estimating-hank-nn
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
```

The last line installs the shared `estimating_hank_nn` package in editable mode, so the
examples can import it and changes to the source take effect without reinstalling. To check
the installation and see which accelerators PyTorch can use, run

```bash
python -c "import torch, estimating_hank_nn; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.backends.mps.is_available())"
```

Then open `examples/rank/rank_baseline.py` in VS Code, select the `estimating-hank-nn`
environment as the kernel, and run the cells in order.

The New Keynesian examples run on a CPU, except Extension 10, which defaults to CUDA. An
NVIDIA GPU (`"cuda"`) or an Apple GPU (`"mps"`) speeds up training, and
[Extension 10](rank/extension-10.qmd) shows how to select one. Training the heterogeneous agent
models needs an NVIDIA GPU, but their saved networks let you reproduce the results on a laptop.
